records.question: What population density range defines the 'intermediate' watershed class?
ground_truth_chunks: From population density data, four watershed classes were defined: pristine (<100 individuals/mi<sup>2</sup> ), minimal (>100 but less than 500 individuals/mi<sup>2</sup> ), intermediate (>500 but less than 1000 individuals/mi<sup>2</sup> ), and extensive (>1000 individuals/mi<sup>2</sup> ).

records.question: What is the population of Tutuila?
ground_truth_chunks: With 55,414 people, Tutuila is the most densely populated island (average density=1045 individuals/mi<sup>2</sup> ).

records.question: What data source and year were used to approximate the level of human disturbance within local watersheds on Tutuila?
records.ground_truth_answer: US Census data from 2000 (Census 2000) downloaded from the Census 2000 website were used to approximate human disturbance.
ground_truth_chunks: Instead, US Census data from 2000 were used to approximate the level of human disturbance within local watersheds.
Data were downloaded from the Census 2000 website (www.census2000.gov).
Watershed populations were calculated by summing village population totals within each watershed (following Pedersen 2000).

records.question: According to the RESULTS section, what population density cutoffs were used to classify watersheds as pristine, minimal disturbance, intermediate disturbance, and extensive modification?
records.ground_truth_answer: Pristine: less than 100 individuals/mi^2. Minimal disturbance: greater than 100 but below 500 individuals/mi^2. Intermediate disturbance: above 500 but less than 1000 individuals/mi^2. Extensive modification: around (at or above) 1000 individuals/mi^2.
ground_truth_chunks: The break in the distribution of the first group was arbitrarily set at 100 individuals/mi<sup>2</sup> . Watersheds below that density point were considered **pristine**.

This was an arbitrary decision, but, in lieu of other supporting data to more carefully distinguish among these watersheds, this decision was acceptable. Thus, below the 500 individuals/mi<sup>2</sup> but greater than 100 individuals/mi<sup>2</sup> , watersheds were considered as showing **minimal** disturbance. Above 500 but less than 1000 individuals/mi<sup>2</sup> , units were classified as showing **intermediate** disturbance.
The major break at around 1,000 individuals/mi<sup>2</sup> marked the transition into watersheds showing **extensive** modification.

records.question: What population density threshold marks the upper boundary of watersheds considered 'pristine' in the classification scheme?
ground_truth_chunks: The first break, set arbitrarily at 100 individuals/mi<sup>2</sup> , marks the upper boundary of watersheds considered pristine.

records.question: What percentage of the perennial stream basins on Tutuila are less than 1 km^2?
records.ground_truth_answer: 122/141 (87%) of the perennial stream basins are less than 1 km^2.
ground_truth_chunks: There are 163 streams on Tutuila, 141 of which are considered perennial (Burger and Maciolek 1981).
Specifically, 122/141 (87%) of the perennial stream basins are less than 1 km<sup>2</sup> .
